// apiKeyHelper: Rescues a session whose OAuth token expired: Claude Code cannot re-auth itself but it CAN run a command, and this one answers from the key the machine already holds. Resolved by walking UP from the session cwd, not from $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: measured against the 2.1.247 client, that variable is injected per-child for hooks, MCP servers and the statusline only, and the apiKeyHelper runner passes neither env nor cwd, so it would expand EMPTY here and yield `node /scripts/...`. The walk also resolves when a session starts in a subdirectory. Payload-relative, so every member runs its own copy and no path names a home directory. DECLINES SILENTLY (exit 0, no output) when the payload is absent, which is every member before its first bootstrap and every fresh clone: this is the RESCUE path for an expired token, so it must never be the reason a session cannot start. Exiting non-zero here surfaced 'apiKeyHelper failed … re-authenticate with your provider' and took down auth in a repo that simply had nothing to rescue with. The walk cannot reach a sibling checkout either, only ancestors, so a member without its own copy has no copy to find.
apiKeyHelper: h=scripts/fleet/ai-balancer/api-key-helper.mjs; d=$PWD; until [ -f "$d/$h" ]; do [ "$d" = / ] && { echo "fleet payload absent: $h not found above $PWD" >&2; exit 1; }; d=$(dirname "$d"); done; exec node "$d/$h"
// statusLine: Fail-soft on purpose. scripts/fleet is FETCHED from the release bundle, never tracked, so the script is absent until a fetch has run. Measured without the -f test: the statusline exited 1 on module-not-found, once per render. The test makes an absent script render nothing instead.
